steps.title: Privilege gateway
steps.what: User Token is documented to send the credential in the user's Privilege vault, and nothing if the vault is empty.
steps.why: Backends need a credential the gateway can send, but the caller's own gateway key must never reach the backend.

steps.title: Privilege console: Add and Edit application,…
steps.what: Each MCP Server or Remote Agent application has an Auth Mode that decides what the backend receives after sign-in and policy pass.
steps.why: Backends need a credential the gateway can send, but the caller's own gateway key must never reach the backend.

steps.title: Static Token field on the application
steps.what: Static Token sends a configured bearer token.
steps.why: Backends need a credential the gateway can send, but the caller's own gateway key must never reach the backend.

steps.title: Gateway log
steps.what: The caller's gateway key is never forwarded.

steps.title: Token pass-through
steps.what: A fifth mode, token pass-through, has a front-end application acting as an agent mint a short-lived signed assertion naming the end user, itself and the target backend; the gateway verifies it and forwards it unchanged.
steps.why: Backends need a credential the gateway can send, but the caller's own gateway key must never reach the backend.
